full_judgment:
2. The background leading to the Rule, in short, is that the petitioner opened L/C of US $ 66,00,000 and LTR loan 2,85,000 and time to time renewed and enhanced the loan and subsequently failed to repay to dues. Consequently respondent No.2, the Manager, NCC Bank Motijheel C/A, Dhaka filed Title Suit No. 131 of 2007 in the Court of Artha Rin Adalat No.3, Dhaka (herein after referred to as Adalat) impleading the petitioner and others as defendant for realization of the dues of Taka 95,90,995.04. The suit was decreed exparte on 13- 10-2004. Respondent bank then put the decree into execution by Execution Case No. 34 of 2009 on 15-3-2009 for realization of outstanding dues. On 28-5-2009 the respondent Bank filed an application for issuing warrant of arrest against the petitioner and the Adalat passed the Order of Warrant of arrest on the same dated but the Order was not executed .Then again on 3-3-2011 the respondent Bank filed an application for issuing warrant of arrest and on the same dated the Artha Rin Adalat issued Order of further warrant of arrest. At this stage the petitioner moved this Division and obtained the present Rule and stay of the Order of the warrant of arrest. 

 4. That in violation of Rule 37 of Order XXI and section 56 of the Code of Civil Procedure without issuing any show cause notice the respondent No.1 Artha Rin Adalat issued warrant of arrest which is without any lawful authority and is of no legal effect. Next he contends that as per provision of section 56 of the Code of Civil Procedure the Court shall not issue Order of arrest or detention in the Civil prison of a woman in execution of a decree for the payment of money but without following the said mandatory provision of the Ain, the Adalat most illegally issued the Order of warrant of arrest which cannot be sustained. He further submits that this has also been done in violation of principle of natural justice and is violative of fundamental right as enshrined in the Constitution. The learned counsel placed reliance on the decision of Hazera Begum vs Artha Rin Adalat reported in 5 ADC 220 in support of his contention. Citing the said decision the learned counsel submits that our Appellate Division considering various provisions of Artha Rin Adalat Ain. 1990 and section 56 of the Code of Civil Procedure in particular held that section 56 of the Code civil Procedure is applicable in Artha Rin Adalat Ain 1990 and warrant of arrest cannot be issued against a woman for that matter. He has also brought to our notice that the Appellate Division passed its decision in the year 2007 when the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 was in operation. Therefore, as the learned counsel submits, in all fairness this Rule should be made absolute as per decision of the Appellate Division as referred to above. 

 9. In the case of Hazera Begum vs Artha Rin Adalat 54 DLR 78 the High Court Division had decided that a woman could be arrested and detained in civil prison by Artha Rin Adalat in execution of a decree in view of section 6(Ka) of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 1990. But that decision ultimately in the year 2007 had been repealed by the Appellate Division in 5 ADC 220 as referred to above. In so doing our Appellate Division took into account the different provisions of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 1990 in particular section 5(4), (5) section 6(Ka) read with section 55, 56 and Order 21 of the code of civil procedure and [many decided:- 

 "It is noticed that even the concerned Adalat has passed the Order complained of issuing warrant of arrest and detention of the appellant in civil prison pursuant to Order XXI, Rule 37 read with section 55 of the Code. The legislature in enacting section 6(ka) has not excluded the application of sections 55, 56 and Order XXI and the Rules made thereunder except Rules 5,6, 7, 8 and 9 relating to transfer of decree to some other forum for execution. Since section 5 (4) and 5 (5) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 1990 has clothed the Artha Rin Adalat with the power to exercise its jurisdiction as a Civil Court following the provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure in so far as it is not inconsistent with any provision of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, the legislature was required to make express provision in section 6 (Ka) to exclude the operation of section 56 of the Code of Civil Procedure, but it was not done so. Section 6(Ka) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 1990 cannot, therefore, be construed to exclude the operation of section 56 of the Code of Civil Procedure in matters of execution of any decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat. Any other construction of section 6(Ka) would lead to absurdity and cause failure of justice. The impugned judgment and Order passed by the learned Judges of the High Court Division is therefore erratic and perverse." 

 "It appears that the section 34 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 is clear and provides for Ordering civil imprisonment up to 6 months against a judgment-debtor for compelling to satisfy the decree. Section-34 is not dependent upon Section-33. In the instant case, the decree holder has taken step for auction sale of the property but there being no response, auction sale could not be held. Further it appears from the provisions of Section 34 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 that the law provides for simple civil imprisonment of the judgment-debtor to compel.to make the payment for satisfaction of the decree and is not an alternative punishment in lieu of payment of the decretal amount. Civil imprisonment will not exempt payment of the decretal amount." 

 "However, in view of the specific provision of section 34 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain 2003 relating to the civil imprisonment section 56 Of the Code will not be applicable in execution of the decree of Artha Rin Adalat."
